claim: Mammalian transcription factor genes (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-myc) can induce partially reprogrammed pluripotent stem cell (PRPSC) state in non-mammalian vertebrates (birds and fish) and invertebrates (Drosophila).
source_text: Here we found that a set of four mammalian transcription factor genes used to generate iPSCs in mouse and humans can induce a partially reprogrammed pluripotent stem cell (PRPSCs) state in vertebrate and invertebrate model organisms, in mammals, birds, fish, and fly, which span 550 million years from a common ancestor.
evidence_reasoning: The claim is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript showing transformation of cells from multiple species using the four mammalian genes.

Furthermore, all four genes had highly conserved DNA binding domains
